answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with per-identity proof-of-stake admission: each new agent must lock a ferrous-hard bond of real value before it may transact. Identities are just a cipher to the protocol, so cloning costs nothing until the bond makes every clone pay the same toll, turning one cheap attack into N locked deposits. Peers only count stake-backed votes, so a fable of a thousand agents is only as strong as the capital behind it. An attacker who floods the ledger with fake accounts must fund every one or forfeit to slashing.
